item.title: Official Launch of the Buffalo All Access Pilot Project
item.description: The Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus (BNMC) has officially rolled out its new Buffalo All Access app that links the BNMC neighborhood with access to free, automated community shuttles. The Buffalo All Access pilot project – managed by ADASTEC – launched earlier this month, by introducing the first fully automated, on-demand public shuttle at the BNMC. item.title: Hospitality Study Recommends New 400-Room Downtown Hotel
item.description: In response to a comprehensive tourism market study conducted by HVS (a leading hospitality consulting firm), Visit Buffalo is recommending that a new full-service, 400+ room convention center hotel be considered. item.title: City Opts Out of Paying for Costs Associated with Decimated Former St. Ann’s School
item.description: On January 15, the Buffalo suffered another big preservation setback due to a four-alarm fire that gutted the former St. Ann’s School on Emslie Street (learn more). Since that time, the City has been contemplating what the future of the site holds, with Mayor Sean Ryan officially stating that the owner will ultimately be responsibility for the costs associated with either rehabilitating or demolishing the structure. item.title: Big Reveal: Roswell Health Center Expansion
item.description: Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center’s Community Outreach & Engagement Center that opened in 2023 is growing. New York State Senator April N.M. item.title: Possible Salvation for At-Risk Kenmore Presbyterian Church Structure?
item.description: There’s good news on the Kenmore Presbyterian Church preservation front. When the owners – a Rochester-based group – proposed demolishing the architecturally significant structure to make way for a Shake Shack, the preservation community was aghast. The intent-to-demolish immediately caught the attention of Preservation Buffalo Niagara (PBN), which soon-after went to work on coming up with a tactic to rescue the former church. item.description: Erie County Parks, Recreation & Forestry has rolled out its Commemorative Tree Program, where people can memorialize a loved one by purchasing a tree, to be planted in their name.
